title: Fading Light — Compare the same burst under two clocks and two decay rules
help: Each first flash retains ninety-eight percent over thirty logical updates at the reference rate. Per-second decay adjusts the fraction per update when the rate changes. Two extra pulses still arrive every twenty-four updates, so their spacing in seconds changes. The third choice keeps the raw fraction per update instead. Read update ninety-six; this is lamp level, not exposure.
rows: Sixty updates with fixed fraction per update
message: bursts experiments keep their distinct rules and exact supplied choices
facts: effectiveRetention=.98**(30/rate). Train x0=.35,xn=min(1,r*x(n-1)+pulse),pulse=.35 on24/48 only. Compare at96. Spacing seconds=.8/.4/.4; chart time3.2/1.6/1.6seconds. notes: At thirty updates per second, update ninety-six is 3.20 logical seconds. The two extra pulses are 0.80 seconds apart; the retained train level there is 26.48 percent.
At sixty updates per second with decay per second fixed, update ninety-six is 1.60 logical seconds. Pulses are 0.40 seconds apart; the retained train level there is 51.74 percent.

At sixty updates per second with fraction per update fixed, update ninety-six is still 1.60 logical seconds. The train level is 26.48 percent, like the thirty-update recipe, but it reaches that sample sooner.
